problem_statement: The TailAdmin eCommerce operations dashboard runs a 'Revenue delivery review flow': its dashboard hosts a 'Delivery Review Queue' table where each revenue order carries a product-image proof, an owner handoff, a revenue figure, and a delivery state (Review ready / SLA risk / Needs asset fix). The queue table has its own native status filter: a row of All states / Review ready / SLA risk / Needs asset fix tabs above the delivery rows, plus a live '.dqfilter__readout' count that reports how many of the five orders are showing ('Showing N of 5 . State'). The same 'Delivery review filter' bar is promoted on the Client Delivery Review page so reviewers see the filter on both surfaces of the flow. The filter feature has regressed on four orthogonal axes and must be restyled/repaired together. (1) The filter tab row is laid out as a fixed-width, non-wrapping flex track, so on a 390px mobile viewport it is wider than the phone screen and the whole page overflows horizontally. (2) The filter bar is no longer promoted on the Client Delivery Review page (it is present only on the dashboard). (3) The filtered delivery queue has broken layout: instead of a tidy legible table the rows are pulled together with negative margins so they shingle and overlap into an illegible pile, and the filter tabs, count readout, and status pills are styled as near-white text on near-white fills so they are unreadable. (4) Clicking a status tab marks the tab active but leaves the queue unfiltered and the '.dqfilter__readout' count stale ('Showing 5 of 5 . All states'), so the post-click state is wrong. Restyle the filter tab row so it wraps with no mobile overflow, restore the filter bar so it is promoted on both the dashboard and the Client Delivery Review page, restore the tidy legible queue and legible tabs/pills, and wire the tab clicks so the queue re-filters and the readout re-syncs to 'Showing N of 5 . <State>' — all without altering the delivery-queue row data, the surrounding dashboard widgets, the sidebar/header navigation, or the owner Profile content, and while preserving the Tailwind admin design system, dark mode, and the charts/map/metric widgets.
required_content: The 'Delivery review filter' tab row must fit within a 390px mobile viewport so the page no longer overflows horizontally on the dashboard (no_horizontal_overflow within 24px tolerance).
The 'Delivery review filter' bar must be promoted on BOTH surfaces of the flow: the dashboard (index) AND the Client Delivery Review page (basic-tables). It must not be shown on only the dashboard.

The filtered delivery queue must render as a tidy, legible table (no shingled/overlapping rows), and the filter tabs, count readout, and status pills must be legible (high-contrast text), matching the captured reference delivery-queue states — not a collapsed overlapping queue with unreadable near-white-on-near-white tabs and pills.

Clicking a status tab (for example SLA risk) must re-filter the queue to show only the matching rows AND re-sync the .dqfilter__readout count to 'Showing N of 5 . <State>' (for example 'Showing 1 of 5 . SLA risk'); marking the tab active is not sufficient.

The five delivery-queue rows (Macbook pro 13", Apple Watch Ultra, iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPad Pro 3rd Gen, Airpods Pro 2nd Gen) with their product-image proofs, owner handoffs, revenue figures, and delivery-state labels must remain exactly as authored; only responsive layout, cross-page presence, queue/tab layout, and filter wiring change.
Desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) keep the delivery queue and the 'Delivery review filter' bar with no horizontal overflow, and the five delivery rows continue to render.
The fix must not regress the sidebar, header, search, revenue chart, customers-demographic map, metric group, the Client Delivery Review table, or the owner Profile page.
design_constraints: Treat this as a restyle/repair of the delivery queue's own status filter (mobile overflow + cross-page presence + queue/tab layout + filter wiring), not a redesign of the dashboard.

Use the existing white/dark rounded-card Tailwind style, brand-500 primary accent, and success/warning/error status pills; keep the delivery-queue rows, their proofs, owners, revenue, and labels unchanged.

The filter tab-row overflow repair and the tidy-queue / legible-tab repair live in src/css/dqfilter.css. The cross-page presence repair lives in src/partials/table/table-06.html (whether the Client Delivery Review page renders the filter bar). The tab-click filter + readout wiring plus the dashboard filter markup live in src/partials/table/table-01.html. Do not alter the delivery-queue row data, the dashboard widgets, or the page structure.

The delivery-queue row content and surrounding dashboard DOM must remain identical to the reference; only the responsive overflow behavior, the pages the filter bar renders on, the queue/tab layout, and the filter wiring change.

Ground the repair in the captured visual states: the reference desktop/mobile delivery-queue screenshots show the 'Delivery review filter' bar with legible tabs over a tidy queue, and after clicking SLA risk the queue shows the single SLA-risk row with the readout 'Showing 1 of 5 . SLA risk'.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial verify the dashboard shell, sidebar, header, charts, map, and mobile layout still render.
desktop_delivery_queue and mobile_delivery_queue verify the repaired dashboard delivery queue, the 'Delivery review filter' bar, its legible tabs, and the tidy legible queue across viewports.
desktop_client_delivery_review verifies the Client Delivery Review page renders the same delivery review data AND that the shared 'Delivery review filter' bar is promoted on that route.
desktop_owner_profile and mobile_owner_profile verify the owner Profile route keeps its identity content and the dashboard shell.

desktop_dqfilter_sla scrolls to the delivery queue, clicks the SLA risk status tab, and verifies the queue re-filters to the single SLA-risk row and the .dqfilter__readout re-syncs to 'Showing 1 of 5 . SLA risk' (the interaction terminal state).
The mobile states (mobile_initial, mobile_delivery_queue, mobile_owner_profile) are the horizontal-overflow discriminator: the reference reports 0 overflow while the fixed-width baseline overflows.

change_completion: The 'Delivery review filter' tab row wraps responsively so the dashboard has no horizontal overflow at 390px (within 24px tolerance).

The filter bar is promoted on both the dashboard and the Client Delivery Review page, the queue renders tidily with legible tabs/pills, and clicking a status tab re-filters the queue and re-syncs the .dqfilter__readout count.
design_consistency: The repaired filter bar and delivery queue keep the existing rounded-card, brand-accent, dark-mode, and status-pill style; the queue is not a collapsed overlapping pile and the tabs/pills are legible.
The change does not replace the dashboard with a new page or introduce disconnected UI surfaces.
responsive: On a 390px mobile viewport the filter tab row fits inside the delivery queue card so the document has no horizontal overflow (within 24px tolerance).
Desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) keep the delivery queue and 'Delivery review filter' bar with 0 overflow.
regression: Sidebar, header, search, revenue chart, customers-demographic map, metric group, Client Delivery Review table, and owner Profile page remain available.
The webpack build/serve continues to work without new dependencies.

metadata.design_goal: use real repo content, media, icons, copy, and data structures without generic dummy surfaces
metadata.source_repo_kind: Webpack + Alpine.js + Tailwind v4 admin dashboard with an eCommerce dashboard, a Client Delivery Review tables page, an owner Profile page, local product/user image assets, and a delivery-review data table with a native status filter.
metadata.selected_repo_reason: TailAdmin/tailadmin-free-tailwind-dashboard-template is a runnable Webpack + Alpine.js + Tailwind v4 admin dashboard; it builds to static output offline and hosts a natural dashboard-genre restyle on the dashboard's own delivery-review queue and its native status filter spanning a mobile-overflow defect, cross-page presence, filtered-queue layout, and tab-click wiring.

author_notes: L4 content-asset-continuity restyle on the TailAdmin tailadmin-free-tailwind-dashboard-template admin dashboard, rebuilt in-place from an L2 restyle so the lever is the dashboard's OWN Delivery Review Queue table and its native status filter (All states / Review ready / SLA risk / Needs asset fix over five real delivery rows with a live count), hardened to fail four orthogonal acceptance gates in the bad solution. Lever 1 (D6 no_horizontal_overflow): the filter tab row uses a fixed-width non-wrapping track that overflows a 390px viewport; the reference wraps it. Lever 2 (D2 dom_assertions, cross-page): the 'Delivery review filter' bar must be promoted on both the dashboard and the Client Delivery Review page; the reference promotes it on both, the baseline and bad only on the dashboard, so the '.dqfilter__title' is missing on the Client Delivery Review route. Lever 3 (D3 visual_regression): the bad filtered queue collapses — the delivery rows shingle with negative margins into an overlapping illegible pile and the tabs/readout/status pills are near-white text on near-white fills — failing pixelmatch/ssim/block fidelity against the tidy reference queue. Lever 4 (D4 interaction_assertions): the bad Alpine component flips the active pill but gates the rows on a frozen shownState and renders a snapshotted readoutFrozen, so after the SLA-risk click the count stays 'Showing 5 of 5 . All states'. Three leg-varying files (src/partials/table/table-01.html, src/partials/table/table-06.html, src/css/dqfilter.css) live in suggested_files; the delivery-queue row data and surrounding dashboard DOM are byte-identical across legs. Built offline as a static webpack build (a measurement-enablement sc-infra.css that relaxes the admin-shell overflow-x clamp so overflow is measurable) with that infrastructure identical across legs. Uses real local product images (src/images/product/product-0N.jpg) and the owner avatar (src/images/user/owner.jpg).
